name: Parshandatha
title: Son of Haman
summary: Parshandatha was the eldest of Haman's ten sons. He was killed along with his brothers when the Jews defended themselves against their enemies in the Persian Empire after King Ahasuerus gave them the right to defend themselves. His death marked the defeat of Haman's plan to exterminate the Jewish people.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Plan to Destroy the Jews
keyEvents.description: Haman, the father of Parshandata, persuaded King Ahasuerus to issue a decree to destroy all the Jews in the Persian Empire. This was the background for the threat Haman's family posed to the Jewish people.

keyEvents.title: Esther's Intervention
keyEvents.description: Queen Esther revealed Haman's evil plan to King Ahasuerus and asked that the Jews be spared. This led to Haman being executed, but the decree against the Jews remained in force.

keyEvents.title: The Jews' Right to Self-Defense
keyEvents.description: King Ahasuerus issued a new decree granting the Jews the right to defend themselves against anyone who attacked them. This created the conditions for the battle in which Parshandata and his brothers were killed.

keyEvents.title: Parshandata and His Brothers Are Killed
keyEvents.description: When the Jews defended themselves against their enemies in the fortress of Susa, they killed among others Haman's ten sons, including Parshandata, who is mentioned first in the list. This happened on the thirteenth day of the month of Adar.

keyEvents.title: Haman's Sons Are Hanged
keyEvents.description: At Queen Esther's request, King Ahasuerus ordered that Haman's ten sons, including Parshandata, be hanged on poles. This happened the day after they were killed in battle.

keyEvents.title: The Feast of Purim Is Established
keyEvents.description: In memory of the Jews' victory over their enemies, including the defeat of Haman's family, the feast of Purim was established as an annual celebration among the Jewish people.
